full_judgment:
3. Defendant Nos. 1-3 and 5-7 contested the suit by filing a joint written statement denying all the material allegations made in the plaint contending inter alia, that the suit is not maintainable in its present form; the suit is barred by limitation and it has no cause of action. It was also alleged that the suit has not been filed by the plaintiff but it is filed by putting thumb impression of her son Mahbub. The suit property was gifted by Nawab Ali in favour of his son Md Muslim by deed of gift No. 4073 dated 6-7-1969 and delivered possession of the same to him. The said Md Muslim while in possession and enjoyment of the suit property sold the same to the defendant, Abdul Jabbar, predecessor of the petitioners by a registered deed dated 15-12-1985 and delivered possession of the same. After purchase the said Abdul Jabbar got his name mutated in the khatian and have been in possession by giving boundary wall and barb wire fencing, the story of inclusion of the property in the deed of the plaintiff is false, baseless and fraudulently created for filing of this suit. 

 8. Mr Alam further submits that the question has arisen between the two deeds of gift as to which one shall prevail as per provision of law. Referring to the evidences in respect of both the gift (exhibits-2 and exhibit-A) adduced by the plaintiff in suit, he submits that the plaintiff in his deposition clearly stated that the deed of gift (exhibit-A) was written and executed in the house of the plaintiff and the deed of gift (exhibit 2) written and executed in the registry office which proved that the deed of gift executed in favour of Muslim was earlier one and registration of the same also made before the deed of gift of the plaintiff as appeared from time of registration and serial number of the deed. As such, as per provision of Section 47 of the Registration Act the deed of gift No. 4073 dated 7-6-1969 shall prevail over the deed of gift executed in favour of the plaintiff. He further submits that the plaintiff in suit failed to prove her case by any evidence that after making gift in her favour she got delivery of possession and subsequent record of right stands prepared in her name and she paid rent to the government. But on the other hand the petitioner as defendant adduced evidence in favour of his possession in the suit land, submitted B.S khatian in his vendor's name, got his name mutated in khatian and rent receipts showing payment of rent to the government. 

 16. On the other hand the defendant by oral evidence and by submitting BS khatian in the name of his vendor, rent receipts showing payment of rent and the mutation khatian standing in his name could prove that the defendant is in possession of the suit land measuring 9½ sataks and observed that plaintiff has failed to establish her title by way of gift and adverse possession. 

 18. The trial court while dismissing the suit left no evidence both oral and documentary untouched and undicussed, but the appellate court while allowing the appeal and remanding the suit for rehearing though rightly observed that the plaintiff did not pray for cancellation of the deed or declaring the deed of gift executed in favour of defendant No. 8, Mulsim has not been acted upon in respect of the suit land and did not claim that the khatian has been wrongly recorded in the name of Muslim but wrongly observed that the trial court failed to give decision and findings on each issue framed by the court and also held that the court below failed to frame issue on adverse possession and give any finding on that issue. But in fact the plaintiff has no case of adverse possession in her plaint as well as in the evidences adduced before the court. Therefore, there was no need of framing any issue on adverse possession by the trial court. The appellate court also failed to appreciate the provision of law and held that the trial court only relying on the timing of registration of the deed considered deed of gift of the defendant No. 8, but from the observation of the trial court it appears that the trial court not only considered time of registration of the deed, but also considering the time of execution of both the deeds held that the deed of the defendant No. 8 shall prevail over the deed of the plaintiff.
